version_notes: v4 Table 1 == v3 Table 1 (all 56 method rows identical, checked programmatically).
v4 Tables 10/11/12/13 == v3 Tables 10/11/12/13 (MD/MB fine-tuning numbers unchanged).

protocol.decoding: greedy, POMO multi-start + 8x dihedral (symmetric) augmentation, best of n x 8 solutions per instance (Sec. 5 'Evaluation'; App. B.3)
protocol.gap_reference: HGS-PyVRP ('*' = best-known solutions); OR-Tools also reported
protocol.classical_time_limit: single CPU core per instance, 10 s (n=50) / 20 s (n=100), parallelised over 16 cores (Sec. 5 'Baselines')
protocol.time_column: total wall time for the 1000 instances
protocol.hardware: eval on AMD Ryzen Threadripper 3960X + single RTX 3090
protocol.training: 300 epochs x 100k instances, Adam lr 3e-4, batch 256, lr x0.1 at epochs 270 and 295; MB and MD excluded from training

main_table_16.note: RF-TE is the best neural method on all 16 variants at n=100 in RF's own table. The 24-variant (incl. 8 MB) and 48-variant sets are not in Table 1; MB/MD variants appear only in the fine-tuning Tables 3, 10-13 (n=100 only, obj to 2 decimals, no time column).

mixed_backhaul_8_variants.note: '∅' = zero-shot evaluation. Same fine-tuning budget as MD (10 epochs x 10k instances).

source.table: Table 12 (App. D.7.1); EAL/AL/scratch rows identical to main-text Table 3

single_variant_pomo_finetune.note: EAL fine-tuning of single-variant POMO models vs RouteFinder on the 8 MD+MB variants; RouteFinder row = EAL row of Table 12. Not transcribed per-variant.

source.table: Table 11 (App. D.7.1, p.38); identical in v3 Table 11

setting.depots: m=3 depots (App. A.1: 'we employ m = 3 depots for the MD finetuning variants')
setting.problem_size: n=100 customers -- NOT stated explicitly in Sec. D.7; inferred (HGS MDCVRP 11.89 vs CVRP n=100 15.628 / n=50 10.372; App. D.1 says those experiments are on n=100). Flag as inferred.
setting.test_instances: 1,000 per variant (Table 3 caption 'Finetuning performance on 1,000 ...'; Table 11 caption does not restate it)
setting.gap_reference: HGS-PyVRP ('*'); MD-specific time limit not restated; the only stated PyVRP budget is 20 s/instance for n=100 (Sec. 5 Baselines). OR-Tools also given.
setting.decoding: same as main experiments: greedy multi-start (for MD the first action is forced to start from all depots, App. B.3) + 8x dihedral augmentation
setting.finetune_budget: 10 epochs, 10,000 instances sampled per epoch (Sec. 5.3 and D.7.1). Learning rate / batch size for fine-tuning NOT separately stated; 'similarly to the main experiments' (main: Adam lr 3e-4, wd 1e-6, batch 256).
setting.init: AL and EAL continue from the RF-TE checkpoints of Sec. 5.1; 'Train (scratch)' = untrained RF-TE trained with the same 10x10k budget
setting.eal_md_details: B.4.2: global embedding unchanged; context embedding W_c' gets l=2 zero-initialised rows for origin-depot coords [x_o, y_o]

eal_md.figure_only: Figure 7(b) (main text) plots validation gap averaged across MD tasks vs fine-tuning epoch 0..10 for EAL/AL/Scratch (y-axis 10-35 %). It is validation data, not test; the test numbers are in Table 11, so no read-off was needed.
eal_md.no_average_row_in_paper: RouteFinder does not print an average over the 16 MD variants; all averages here are computed_by_us (unweighted mean of the 16 per-variant gaps).

source.table: Table 9 (App. H, zero-shot on 32 unseen variants, n=100)

other_papers_on_same_RF_MD_test_set.note: Only paper found that reports NEW methods on RouteFinder's own MD test set (its PyVRP, OR-Tools, MTPOMO, MVMoE, RouteFinder rows are copied verbatim from RF Tables 10-12). ZERO-SHOT only, no fine-tuning. 'Ours' = POLAR training + PLE encoder (Correa et al., preprint, Aug 2026).

eal_md.conclusion: No paper found that reports EAL-style (or any) FINE-TUNING numbers on RouteFinder's 16 MD variants other than RouteFinder itself (Table 11). Best published fine-tuned MD number = RF EAL, avg 8.58 % (computed_by_us) after 10 epochs x 10k instances. Best published zero-shot on the same MD test set = POLAR+PLE 21.39 % avg (computed_by_us, 2608.24859 Table 9).

our_reproduction_mapping.verdict: Your believed values 72.145 / 23.282 / 73.010 are exactly the v2 (ICLR camera-ready) ACVRP RRNCO cells. The mapping of repo file names to paper columns is inferred from cost agreement (README only says the three files 'correspond to the ones used in the paper').

rrnco.is_RRNCO_SoTA: Within its own Table 1 (v1 and v2) RRNCO is the best neural method in all 9 cells (best non-RRNCO neural: MatNet for ATSP/ACVRP; ReLD-MoEL (v2) or MVMoE (v1) for ACVRPTW in-dist/OOD-city; GOAL for ACVRPTW OOD-cluster); classical LKH3/PyVRP are better in every cell and OR-Tools beats RRNCO on ACVRPTW. BUT RADAR (ICLR 2026) beats RRNCO in all 9 cells on the same test sets (see radar_on_rrnco_benchmark).

radar_on_rrnco_benchmark.title_verified: RADAR: Learning to Route with Asymmetry-aware DistAnce Representations
radar_on_rrnco_benchmark.protocol: same RRNCO train/test sets (1280 instances of size 100), x8 aug, batch 32; baselines (GCN, MatNet, RRNCO) copied from RRNCO v1 Table 1; gaps given to 2 decimals
radar_on_rrnco_benchmark.note: RADAR's ACVRPTW comparison uses RRNCO v1 (122.693 ...); RADAR still beats RRNCO v2 (122.466 / 122.986 / 40.937).

notes: All 'computed_by_us' averages are unweighted means of the per-variant published gap percentages ('*' counted as 0). Our parsers reproduce every average that papers print in text (MoSES: 2.782/2.631/3.125/2.063; FiLMMeD 24-MD: 4.717/4.740/6.847/6.433; POLAR Table 9 all-32 row; CaDA Fig. 3 bars), which validates the extraction.
Per-variant tables were extracted with pdftotext -layout and parsed programmatically; every parsed 16-variant table was checked so that its HGS-PyVRP objective column equals RF Table 1 exactly.

Best published average gap on RouteFinder's 16-variant n=100 test set (all computed_by_us from per-variant tables): CCL† 1.909 % (ICLR 2026, uses test-time refinement + ReLD), POLAR+PLE 2.102 % (preprint Aug 2026), CCL 2.245 %, FiLMMeD-CaDA† 2.351 %, FiLMMeD-CaDA 2.498 %, MoSES(CaDA) 2.631 %, CaDA 2.814 %, RF-TE 3.124 % (RF own table). At n=50: CCL† 1.100 %, POLAR+PLE 1.192 %.
RF Table 1 vs CaDA/FiLMMeD/POLAR re-evaluations differ slightly for baseline rows (e.g. RF-TE CVRP n=100 1.505 % in RF vs 1.524 % in CaDA); use each paper's own rows when comparing within that paper.
MVMoE and MTPOMO papers use their own test sets/generators (different HGS objectives), so their own tables are not comparable to RF's test set.
RouteFinder MD fine-tuning problem size (n=100) is inferred, not stated; MD HGS time limit not restated; fine-tuning lr not stated separately.

arXiv IDs 2402.16891, 2405.01029, 2412.00346, 2503.16159, 2406.15007 were verified by title on the abs pages; the user-supplied RRNCO title 'Neural Combinatorial Optimization for Real-World Routing' is the v1 title; v2 is 'RRNCO: Towards Real-World Routing with Neural Combinatorial Optimization'.
